_comment: Ground truth for the critique calibration corpus. Each case was written
by hand, critiqued for real, and its findings checked against the code
or against git's actual behaviour before being labelled here.
The corpus is deliberately unbalanced: seven must-fail and one must-pass.
Failures alone cannot detect over-loosening -- a rubric that passed
everything would look identical to one that passed nothing if the corpus
had no positive case. Case 08 is that control. Case 01 is the floor: it is
session-dependent and unverifiable, so any change that lets it pass has
broken the gate regardless of what else improves.
Case 07 was labelled the control and later relabelled must-fail, because
the model found a real defect in it that I had missed. Recording that here
rather than quietly editing it: the corpus is only worth anything if its
ground truth is honest about having been wrong once. It is also the reason
case 08 exists and why every claim in 08 was measured before it was written.

01-fix-the-flaky-check.why: Steps reference 'the same fix we used last time' and 'the way we discussed'. A fresh instance has neither. Verification is 'confirm the check is no longer flaky' -- nondeterministic, no command, no threshold.

02-verify-skillforge-suites.why: Step 2 says repeat for every tests/test_*.py, but the verification re-runs only test_ledger.py, so skipping step 2 still passes. The verification is weaker than the procedure it checks.

03-ledger-schema-change.why: The Verification claims the suite asserts a 'renamed column', but the procedure is about views and tables generally, not renaming. It also never says whether a brand-new view needs a migration.

04-hook-drafting-guard.why: Warns the suite will not discover a new test but never says how to add one, leaving the reader to guess. The verification is therefore uncoupled for the new-hook case the description claims.

05-hook-inert-guard-v3.why: Instructs adding the test, so it is closer -- but the description still claims the new-hook case, where skipping the whole procedure leaves the suite passing. Genuine coupling gap.

06-commit-trailer-unquoted.why: verification.command is unquoted, so the shell reads <noreply@anthropic.com> as a stdin redirect and > as a stdout redirect, TRUNCATING .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG -- the very file it claims to check. A rubric that misses this is not worth running.

07-commit-trailer-fixed.why: Originally labelled the control. That was my error. Its Verification asserts 'run before step 1 it exits 1, because the previous message has no such line' -- false in a repository that already follows the convention, where .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG holds a prior message that already contains the trailer, so grep exits 0 before the procedure runs. A later run found exactly that and graded it textual/blocking, correctly. The earlier failure I disproved was a DIFFERENT, false claim about the file surviving the next commit; both objections targeted the same sentence, one wrongly and one rightly.

08-gitignore-entry.why: Every factual claim was measured before writing it: in a scratch repo, `git check-ignore -q build/` exits 1 before the .gitignore line is added and 0 after. Narrow scope, stated preconditions, and a verification genuinely coupled to the one step the procedure performs. This is the positive control case 07 was supposed to be.

09-gitignore-entry-v2.why: Case 08 with exactly the three defects the model found fixed: the >> newline hazard, the over-general claim that check-ignore exits 1 beforehand (now established by step 1 rather than asserted universally), and the substitute-after-the-command ordering. If this still fails on new valid objections, convergence in a bounded number of rounds is not achievable and critique should not be the automatic promotion criterion.
